title: A standard ranked game, stage by stage

player.name: Keane
player.about: Long-standing Challenger streamer with calm, methodical ranked play. His edited games are chaptered by stage, which makes them a clean model of a standard tempo game.

summary: A ranked game on patch 18.1c edited into stage chapters (stage 1, 3, 4, 5, 6). No gimmick and no high-roll: a standard tempo game from a Challenger player, which is exactly what a climbing player should copy first.
thesis: Most LP is won by doing the standard things on time: strongest board in stage 2, level 6 at 3-2 and 7 at 4-1, two items slammed early, a scout before every fight from stage 4, and gold turned into placement at 5-1. This game is a checklist you can watch. Pause at each chapter, write what you would do, then compare.

timeline.title: Opening: pairs, components, first board
timeline.watch: The first carousel pick and what the stage-1 shops buy: pairs over strength, and a board at level 3 and 4 that fields upgrades as they land. Note which components are combined first.
timeline.why: Stage 2 is decided by pairs and by two early slams; the exact comp is irrelevant until 3-2.
timeline.question: Which two components would you combine first with his stage-2 board, and on whom?

timeline.title: The first augment against a stage-2 board
timeline.watch: Whether the pick is econ, strength or trait, and how it fits a board that has not picked a line yet.
timeline.why: At 2-1 the safest picks keep options open: gold, items, or generic combat. A trait pick this early is a commitment.

timeline.title: Level 6 at 3-2 and the 50-gold floor
timeline.watch: Level 6 at 3-2, no roll, gold climbing toward 50 by 3-5. Watch how the shop is used: copies of what he owns, nothing speculative.
timeline.why: Interest and the level timing are the two habits that separate Silver from Platinum; stage 3 is where both are tested.
timeline.question: How much gold does he have at 3-5, and how much interest did that earn over the stage?

timeline.title: The direction is picked from items and 2-costs
timeline.watch: Which line the board leans toward at 3-2 and what decided it: the items on the board, the 2-star 2-costs, the augment. Not the tier list.
timeline.why: Committing at 3-2 from what you have is how you avoid contest and pivots later.

timeline.title: Level 7 at 4-1, the rolldown, level 8
timeline.watch: The 4-1 level, whether he rolls at 7 or goes to 8 first, and the stop condition. Count the gold left after the roll and the HP that decided the depth.
timeline.why: The 4-1 rolldown is the most expensive decision of the game; its size is set by HP and by the odds at the level you roll at.

timeline.title: Scouting before every fight
timeline.watch: How often the camera leaves his board before a fight from 4-1 on, and what changes after: a swapped carry, a moved tank, a bait unit.
timeline.why: Scouting that does not change a decision was not scouting. Every look should move something or confirm the layout.
timeline.question: Pick one fight in stage 4: what would you have moved after seeing the opponent's board?

timeline.title: Gold into placement
timeline.watch: At 5-1: level 9 or roll at 8, and what the gold buys first: 2-stars of the carries already on the board before any 5-cost.
timeline.why: Once the top 4 is safe, gold turns into placement by two-starring what you have; a 1-star 4-cost is weaker than the 2-star 3-cost it replaced.

timeline.title: Endgame: the placement on the table
timeline.watch: Players left, their HP and boards; whether he plays for 1st or locks a placement; the last positioning changes against a known opponent.
timeline.why: With two or three boards left, every fight is against a board you can see. The last free strength is where your units stand.

questions.q: What did he do at 3-2 that a Gold player usually does not?
questions.a: Level to 6 and refuse to roll. Gold players roll at 3-2 for upgrades and arrive at 4-1 without the gold for the real rolldown.

questions.q: How is the size of the 4-1 rolldown decided?
questions.a: By HP (how many losses are affordable), by the odds at the level he rolls at, and by a stop condition chosen before the first roll. Not by what the shop shows.

questions.q: What is the one habit from this game to copy this week?
questions.a: Scout before every fight from 4-1 and move one unit because of it. It costs nothing and it is what the video shows most often.

sourceNote: Title, channel, date, length, the patch (18.1c from the description) and the stage chapter timestamps come from the creator's video page. The stage guide is TFT Lab's reading of a standard tempo game; it tells you what to look for, not what happens at each second.
